chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: If a woman dies, who among the people has the greatest right to perform the salat (prayer) over her? He عليه السلام said: Her husband. I said: Is the husband more entitled concerning her than the father, the child, and the brother? He said: Yes, and he washes her.

key_terms.أَحَقُّ: more entitled; having the strongest legal priority
key_terms.تَمُوتُ: dies; indicating the context of death and funeral rulings
key_terms.زَوْجُهَا: her husband; the one identified as having priority
key_terms.يَغْسِلُهَا: he washes her; referring to performing ghusl for the deceased woman
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer); here, the funeral prayer over the deceased
key_terms.ٱلْأَبِ: the father; mentioned as having less priority than the husband in this case
key_terms.ٱلْمَرْأَةُ: the woman; the deceased female being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.ٱلْوَلَدِ: the child; also mentioned in the order of entitlement

ai.seo_question: Who has the greatest right to perform the funeral prayer over a deceased woman in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states that when a woman dies, her husband has the strongest right to perform the salat (prayer) over her funeral. It further affirms that he has priority over her father, child, and brother, and that he may also wash her body.
